requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
structural: No structural obligation in `requirements.index.chapter` needs implementation evidence. I read the clauses one by one, and each one specifies observable `habeas mdbook` behavior. None prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named interface to delegate to.

- "An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many." This describes the accepted input syntax. A MAY imposes nothing to check. A parser built any other way would accept and reject the same input, so the choice is discretionary.
- "A book MUST contain no more than one such directive." This is a constraint on input books. A different validation mechanism would give the same outcome.
- "`habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page." This is output content. Any rendering code that lists the same requirements and links to the same pages meets it.
- "When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by `requirements.index.chapter.default`." This is a behavioral branch. How the replacement is done, in place or by a preprocessor pass, is not prescribed. The fallback chapter is judged against `requirements.index.chapter.default`, and the detail pages against `requirements.index.detail_pages`. Both are cited as context here, not delegated to as structural interfaces.

There are no review roots and no acknowledgments, and none are needed. The behavior is verified through tests, which are outside this structural assessment.

behavioral: I derived these obligations from `requirements.index.chapter`. Every one has a marked test with assertions that enforce it. I did not reassess `requirements.index.chapter.default` or `requirements.index.detail_pages`. They are cited context here and have their own tests.

- **Directive syntax: standalone, empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` covers these cases:
  - A four-colon open and close is accepted, and the exact range is asserted.
  - A directive inside a code fence or inside a `{req}` example block is ignored.
  - A missing close, a non-empty body, and a close with fewer colons than the open are all errors.
  - A two-colon directive and an inline (non-standalone) one are ignored.
  - A close with more colons than the open is accepted.
- **No more than one directive per book.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two directives in separate chapters and two in one chapter. Both cases assert an error containing "only one".
- **The index lists all requirements and examples defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its detail page.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` checks the following:
  - Every one of five requirements has a row whose link goes to `requirements-index/<name>.html`, including the one with no evidence record.
  - Each row's evidence state is asserted.
  - The table's column alignment is asserted.
  - The detail pages exist under the index chapter.

  `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` adds an example, a requirement in a nested child chapter, and a dotted name. It also checks the links from definitions to detail pages. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` covers an example defined in a separate chapter.
- **A present directive is replaced with the index table.** The explicit-directive tests assert that `{requirements-index}` is gone from the index chapter's content and that the table rows are present. `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` also shows the explicit index keeps its placement, with three top-level items.
- **With no directive, the default chapter is generated.** `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` and `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` assert the appended chapter, its table, and the absence of the marker. The detailed default-chapter properties belong to `requirements.index.chapter.default`.

I found no untested obligation or boundary the text names.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
